topics.name: What is State?
topics.description: Understand graph state and what it is for.

topics.name: MessagesState
topics.description: The built-in state for chat messages.

questions.title: What is the purpose of State in LangGraph?
questions.explanation: State stores data shared across graph nodes. Each node reads the current state and returns updates to it.

questions.title: Which of the following can be used as the state schema of a StateGraph?
questions.explanation: TypedDict is the most common choice, and dataclasses and Pydantic models are also supported. A bare str has no named fields for nodes to update.

questions.title: What does this program print?
questions.codeSnippet:
from typing import TypedDict
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END

class State(TypedDict):
    count: int
    note: str

def inc(state: State) -> dict:
    return {"count": state["count"] + 1}

builder = StateGraph(State)
builder.add_node("inc", inc)
builder.add_edge(START, "inc")
builder.add_edge("inc", END)
graph = builder.compile()

print(graph.invoke({"count": 1, "note": "hi"}))

options.text: An error, because inc does not return the whole state

questions.explanation: A node returns a partial update. Keys it does not return, such as note, keep their previous values.

questions.title: If a state key has no reducer, what happens when a node returns a new value for it?

options.text: The new value is appended to the old one
The new value overwrites the old value
The old value is kept and the update is ignored

questions.explanation: Without a reducer the default behavior is to overwrite the key. Use a reducer to combine values instead.

questions.title: Fill in the blank so that lists returned by different nodes are concatenated.
questions.codeSnippet:
import operator
from typing import Annotated, TypedDict

class State(TypedDict):
    logs: Annotated[list[str], ______]
questions.explanation: The second argument of Annotated is the reducer. operator.add(old, new) concatenates two lists.

questions.title: What does the prebuilt MessagesState provide?

options.text: A messages key that uses the add_messages reducer
A database connection for chat history

questions.explanation: MessagesState is a ready-made state with a messages list annotated with add_messages. It does not execute tools or persist data by itself.

questions.title: How does add_messages merge a returned message into the existing list?

options.text: It always replaces the whole list
It appends new messages and replaces an existing message that has the same ID
It drops all messages except the last one

questions.explanation: add_messages appends new messages and updates a message in place when the ID already exists.

questions.title: The chatbot forgets earlier turns. What is the bug?

options.text: messages has no reducer, so the returned value overwrites the history instead of appending to it

questions.explanation: Annotate the key with a reducer, for example messages: Annotated[list, add_messages], or use MessagesState.
